title: Birth in Austin and early schooling at Sam Houston College
summary: Wilson gives his birthdate and parents' names, his brother Gus, and how his mother taught them to read so they entered school at four and five.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So I guess that a good place to start would be back to my earliest recollections as a child back in Austin, Texas. I was born in Austin, Texas on November 24, 1912, and my father's name was James Augustus Wilson, my mother was Pearl Georgia Shaw, her maiden name.
When I was born, I had one older brother, a year and a half older than me, James Augustus, Jr., after my father -- we call him Gus. His nickname was always Gus for Augustus.
And the first recollections, like maybe

when I was four or five years old in Austin, Texas, where my father and mother were both on the faculty of the Sam Houston College, which in those days, was right there in Austin, and which later merged with the Tillotson School, I guess.
In those days, it was Sam Houston College, and I remember my very, very early schooling there ... learning to read and write --
What did your mother and father teach? The subjects.

My father was the Dean there, the Dean of Men, I believe his job was -- and my mother taught in the elementary grades, and she taught my brother, Gus -- and me, to read and write at home, so we actually entered school in the second grade when we were about four years old, because she had taught us all that material, and in the south, in those days, there was nothing compulsory about having to be six years old to go in the first grade.
So we went right in the fourth grade; I was four and my brother was five at Sam Houston there.
